data.narrative:
Solugen is a Series D-stage climate and energy technology company that has raised $640M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—Redwood Materials ($6.0B Series D), KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $640M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.5x multiplier typical of Series D-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $960M. Peer-median analysis across the four-company cohort produces a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range from $700M to $6.0B. These two approaches bracket the opportunity: stage-progression reflects a conservative floor anchored to capital deployed, while peer-median captures the broader market opportunity.

The triangulated valuation range is $816M (low), $1.5B (median), and $2.3B (high). The wide peer distribution ($700M–$6.0B) reflects heterogeneity in business model maturity and market segments within climate-tech. Key uncertainties include the strength of Solugen's unit economics relative to peers, its path to revenue scale, and sector-level appetite for financing in an evolving regulatory environment.
